narrative.overview:
This is a portfolio that earns attention through restraint, not volume. The visual system treats the screen like a craftsman's bench — dark wood, warm light on metal, nothing that doesn't belong. Every element is placed with the confidence that the work itself carries the weight; design's job is to frame it, not perform for it.

The personality is warm without being soft, competent without posturing. The single geometric sans-serif (Plein) speaks in one voice across all surfaces. Weight and size do the work of hierarchy; nothing decorative intervenes. The palette runs dark-to-light on a single cool axis — deep navy surfaces, a muted blue accent drawn from coastal fog, off-white ink that reads warm against the dark.
keyCharacteristics: Single geometric sans-serif voice with committed weight contrast
Dark surface as the field; off-white ink as the primary text
One accent color, used sparingly (≤10% of any surface)
Tonal layering for depth — no shadows, just color contrast and backdrop-blur
Restrained motion: staggered fade-up entrance on hero only, respects reduced-motion

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Muted Maritime is used on ≤10% of any single surface. Its rarity is the point. If a page has more than one solid-fill Muted Maritime element visible at once, the accent is losing its signal value.

rules.name: The Night-Warm Rule
rules.body: Dark navy (#061f2f) is the only permitted page background. A pure-black background reads cold and defaults to style over substance.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Plein is the only typeface used across the entire site (excluding monospace code tags). No italic display, no serif pairing, no secondary type family.

rules.name: The Light-on-Dark Rule
rules.body: All text on the dark navy surface uses a minimum opacity of 60% (#f0edee at 0.6) — never lower. Light text on dark backgrounds reads as lighter weight; compensate with slightly looser line-height.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest and flat on hover. No box-shadow is permitted in the system. Depth is tonal or it isn't there.

rules.name: The Blur-Only Overlay Rule
rules.body: When an element must float above content (navbar), use backdrop-blur-sm with a semi-transparent background. This is the only permitted overlay technique.

dos: Do use Muted Maritime (#6d98ba) for the one primary CTA per page and for hover/active states.
Do use Developer Blue-Black (#061f2f) as the only page background.
Do keep body text at 70% opacity on dark backgrounds, with line-height 1.6.
Do use text-wrap: balance on all heading elements (h1–h3).
Do respect prefers-reduced-motion: reduce — all animations must degrade.
Do use tonal layering (background opacity + backdrop-blur) for floating elements.
Do cap body line length at 65ch for prose sections.
Do maintain the staggered entrance rhythm (80ms delay per child) for the hero section only.
donts: Don't use flashy, gradient-heavy, or scroll-jacking animations.
Don't use hacker/terminal aesthetics — no green-on-black, no monospace body copy.
Don't use corporate stiffness — no buzzwords, no impersonal copy.
Don't use side-stripe borders as colored accents on cards or alerts.
Don't use gradient text (background-clip: text with gradient).
Don't use numbered section markers as default scaffolding.
Don't use tiny uppercase tracked eyebrows above every section.
Don't use glassmorphism or decorative blurs beyond the navbar's functional backdrop-blur.
Don't lower body text opacity below 60% on dark backgrounds.
Don't add a second accent color beyond Muted Maritime.
